stages.transformation: Retrieved from the ETR package and registered in the Source register with its access status and period range.
stages.doesNotProve: A registered source proves only that the data was retrieved, not that any reading follows from it.

stages.content: Oct 2026: Net Score 38.05, Deployment Breadth (Pervasion) 41.22, N 452
stages.transformation: One survey period recorded exactly as supplied, with its base and respondent cut. No rounding, no interpolation.
stages.doesNotProve: A single period is a measurement, not a trend, and not a company outcome.

stages.transformation: The observation is qualified: given an ID, a confidence, a verification status and a recorded caveat, and linked to the signal it can inform.
stages.doesNotProve: Qualifying evidence does not establish causation or any company financial result.

stages.content: Post-Outage Spending Recovery in ETR TSIS Data — current reading: Net Score 38.05, Deployment Breadth (Pervasion) 41.22, N 452, All Respondents
stages.transformation: Evidence is assembled into a reviewable signal candidate with an explicit confidence, evidence strength and a named list of source gaps.
stages.doesNotProve: Z-Score method bands; cohort/region N; current retention; current shared accounts
stages.detail: Reviewer decision: Pending Review. The recorded signal statement quotes the archived October reading and is kept in the archive; the reading above is the one in force.

stages.content: Q/Q Z-Score 0.129 and Y/Y Z-Score 0.892 are both positive; the Y/Y model output is higher, matching the larger Y/Y base-metric change.
stages.transformation: A reviewer states what the evidence means, under named interpretation rules, with the confidence recorded.
stages.doesNotProve: Statistical significance, approved strength band, economic relevance, or prediction.

stages.content: CrowdStrike’s October demand signal holds: breadth expands while sequential momentum levels off.

stages.doesNotProve: A draft is not an approved output: R-020 makes human review a precondition of distribution.
